segments.note: The first steam locomotive, the Shields, arrived June 15 1832 but proved unreliable; a second engine, the Pontchartrain (built in England), let the line advertise regular steam service of 7 round trips a day (9 on Sundays) starting Sept 27 1832. Its sooty exhaust earned the line the nickname 'Smoky Mary.' Round-trip fare was 75 cents. The railroad turned Milneburg from a working port into a lakeside resort. Headway derived from the 7-9 daily round trips; frequency changes across this long independent era are otherwise estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Leased by the Louisville and Nashville Railroad in 1880 and purchased outright the following year, becoming an L&N branch. One-way fare was 15 cents (25 cents round trip) for much of this era, dropping to 10 cents one-way (5 cents for children) by the early 20th century. The last passenger train ran March 15 1932, ending just over a century of continuous service; L&N kept running freight until 1935 to support the Lakefront land reclamation project that erased Milneburg's shoreline. A single milestone marker on Elysian Fields Avenue is about the only physical trace left today. Frequency for this era estimated, unsourced.

metadata.horsecar_audit: 2026-08-24: removed as part of a repo-wide horsecar audit. Removed here: segment 1831-1832 from pontchartrain-railroad (the opening horse-drawn segment; the feature now begins in 1832 when the line went over to steam). REPO RULE 5: this map shows MECHANICALLY powered rail -- horsecars and mule cars are out of scope, and a line's drawn years must start when it stopped using animals. Notes may still mention the animal era as context. See CLAUDE.md.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
